newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes firm amid dated Brent uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes firm amid dated Brent uncertainty.

text.p: North Sea crude prices edged higher on Wednesday, aided by a firmer Brent market although no Brent deals could be confirmed, traders said.

Forties, Oseberg, Gulfaks C and Draugen barrels were all traded at firmer levels and Dated Brent was rumoured traded as high as Feb Brent evens to +2 cents though neither party would confirm the trade.
Dated Brent was assessed slightly firmer at around March +25/+30 cents in late talk after the only cargo in the paper chains was kept by the equity holder.
"There is a bit of strength in the prompt market. A bit of hype for the moment, but overall it looks black. Margins are poor and buyers are covered," a trader said.
March IPE Brent came under some selling pressure during the afternoon session but bounced back to stand 30 cents up at $22.66 a barrel in late business.
Ekofisk equity holders were still experiencing loading problems with one lifter reportedly deferred on a million barrels for Jan 31-Feb 01 loading to Feb 2-4 and Feb 3-5 slots.
Mid-Feb Oseberg and Forties cargoes were traded around Dated Brent +40 with a Feb 11-13 Gulfaks C sold at +49 and a Feb 13-15 Draugen at +44 cents.
Mar/Apr traded twice at +43 cents and Feb/Mar leapt ahead to move at +38 cents. Both were holding these levels in late business.

CFDs for next week were steady around March Brent +20 cents although levels further out were a little shaky with Feb 3-7 trading at March Brent +15-1/2 cents early but best bids were around +10 cents in late discussion.
In the Mediterranean, Urals buyers were subdued by poor refining margins but, with only one or two end January cargoes left, traders said the next deal might be done as high as dated Brent -65 cents.
"It just depends on whether there is someone there who really needs a cargo in that time range. They might have to pay up," one said.
In the West African market, a range of deals for the past week began to appear in a wide price range.

Traders said S Korean buyers were still in evidence but the premium for gas oil rich grades should erode over the next week or so. Forcados looked under some pressure with end January and early February barrels still on offer. Qua Iboe was assessed around dated +61-63 cents with Brass around dated +65 cents.
There could be further downside ahead, equity holders warned.

"All the excitement was when the East came in to mop up extra barrels and then took more than that. The differentials were brought too high and now with (refinery) runs being talked about they could start to come off," one large player said. --Colin Wooster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7456
